instructions: You build MuJoCo scenes that do what their briefs say, and you check them honestly.

content.text:
No. Ball1 drops through ring1, strikes lever1, and comes to rest by about 1.41 s. The lever strikes cart1 and reaches its 45° stop, but rebounds and settles at 38.3°. Cart1 then hits the domino platform at about 1.23 s, stopping roughly 4 cm short of domino1; the domino is never touched.

The correction moves the platform out of the striker’s path. It also gives the lever a slightly top-heavy mass distribution—without changing its dimensions, mass, or central hinge—so gravity holds it against the lower stop after the strike. This revised file has not been rerun here.

    </body>

         Its center of mass is 8 mm above the hinge: initial gravity torque

    <body name="lever1" pos="0 0 0.30">
      <inertial pos="0 0 0.008" mass="0.50" diaginertia="0.000451333 0.015034667 0.015416667"/>

      <joint name="cart1_slide" type="slide" axis="1 0 0" range="0 0.42" damping="0.20" solreflimit="0.008 1" solimplimit="0.95 0.99 0.001"/>
      <geom name="cart1_chassis" type="box" size="0.11 0.09 0.05" mass="0" friction="0.72 0.005 0.002" condim="6" solref="0.008 0.716" solimp="0.95 0.99 0.001" rgba="0.16 0.65 0.35 1"/>
